The test image shows a corn ear with dark green mold covering the kernels throughout the ear. Key features:
- Dark green/teal colored mold on kernels
- Mold covering the entire ear surface
- Powdery/fuzzy fungal growth between and on kernels
- Husks pulled back revealing the infection

Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Trichoderma** (dark green mold covering entire ear) vs **Ear_rots_Aspergillus** (olive-green to gray-green, typically starting at tip).

Let me view the reference collage to confirm.

The reference images confirm the match. The test image shows dark green mold growing between and on the kernels, covering the entire ear — a perfect match for **Ear_rots_Trichoderma**. The distinctive dark green (almost black) color and whole-ear coverage distinguish it from Aspergillus (olive-green, tip-focused) or Ear_rots_Diplodia (white mold starting at base).
